findings.title: Keep one canonical CPR implementation
findings.impact: Multiple formula representations can drift in thresholds, denominator conventions, or edge-case handling.
findings.evidence: The repository has a canonical contract, plus separate live and breakout adapters that repeat formula-oriented logic and column mappings.
findings.recommendation: Keep numerical math exclusively in cpr_contract.py and test adapters only as compatibility mappings.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A repository test asserts all consumers use calculate_cpr/calculate_cpr_frame and no consumer contains independent CPR arithmetic.

findings.title: History refresh can be made incremental and parallel-safe
findings.impact: A 252-session cache fill can issue many sequential network requests and repeatedly load/concatenate large Pandas panels.
findings.evidence: ensure_bhavcopy_history loops dates sequentially and load_history_panel reads every cached CSV for each scan/backfill path.
findings.recommendation: Add a cache manifest, skip known unavailable holidays, separate acquisition from computation, and benchmark a bounded concurrent downloader with rate limits.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A benchmark records scan time, request count, and memory for 60 and 252 sessions; repeated scans do not re-read unchanged inputs unnecessarily.

findings.title: Generated archive growth should be managed
findings.impact: Daily full tables, shortlist files, caches, and site downloads accumulate indefinitely and increase clone, build, and deployment cost.
findings.evidence: The repository tracks a large date-stamped cpr_output archive and the site builder writes per-date pages and downloads.
findings.recommendation: Define retention tiers, compress archival inputs, avoid duplicating identical exports, and publish a compact manifest/index.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A documented retention policy exists and a year-scale fixture stays within an agreed repository and build-size budget.

findings.title: Separate scan publication permissions from repository write access where possible
findings.impact: A compromised workflow or dependency could modify the repository as well as publish the site.
findings.evidence: The scheduled workflow grants contents: write, pages: write, and id-token: write, and commits generated CSVs.
findings.recommendation: Use a least-privilege design: publish artifacts without write access when possible, or isolate archive commits in a narrowly scoped workflow with pinning and review.
findings.acceptance_criteria: The workflow’s permissions are justified in documentation and a dry-run proves site deployment still works with the minimum required scopes.

findings.title: The current repository is deterministic, not an AI predictor
findings.impact: Calling rule-based scoring or validation AI could mislead users about what the system has learned or forecast.
findings.evidence: The tracked Python source contains CPR formulas, rolling indicators, fixed scoring, and backtests, but no LLM or machine-learning inference pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Keep the reviewer and signal logic explicitly labelled as deterministic. If an LLM reviewer is added, keep it advisory, schema-validated, and separate from signal generation.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Documentation distinguishes deterministic strategy rules, automation, and any future LLM-assisted code review.

findings.title: Keep generated market data out of default review prompts
findings.impact: Large historical CSV archives make code review, cloning, and LLM analysis expensive and can drown out source evidence.
findings.evidence: The repository inventory contains 1664 generated files under cpr_output.
findings.recommendation: Use a manifest plus sampled schemas in review tooling, and consider storing bulky archives in release artifacts or object storage while keeping reproducible fixtures in Git.
findings.acceptance_criteria: The review agent reads schemas and metadata by default, never sends full generated archives to an analysis model, and CI remains reproducible from a small fixture.
